lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Skill model: reading a sample lease and naming its obligations

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic reading a sample lease and naming its obligations task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: A sample lease excerpt is provided for a fictional apartment, Sunrise Apartments.
safetyNotes: The lease excerpt is entirely fictional and provided for this lesson; the learner should not use or reference any real lease or real address.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Which clause in this excerpt is one a first-time tenant might not think to look for, and why does missing it matter?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u04-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Obligation identification accuracy: All four categories are correctly and specifically stated using details from the excerpt. | Tenant vs. landlord distinction: All listed obligations are correctly attributed to tenant or landlord. | Noticing what's easy to miss: Reflection identifies a specific clause and gives a plausible reason it's easy to miss. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Provide the learner with a second, slightly more complex lease excerpt that adds a clause the first one didn't have (such as a pet deposit or an early-termination fee) and have them name that new obligation and which party it falls on.

resources.title: reading a sample lease and naming its obligations coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: A sample lease excerpt is provided for a fictional apartment, Sunrise Apartments.
Coach direction: Before reading the sample lease, write your own working definition of the key term.
Learner prompt: Before reading the sample lease, what do you think the word 'obligation' means in the context of an agreement like a lease?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: reading a sample lease and naming its obligations complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Work through the sample lease excerpt in four parts, writing exactly what it states for each.
Response 1 (t2-p1): Payment terms: what is the rent amount, when is it due, and what happens if it's paid late?
Response 2 (t2-p2): Deposit terms: how much is the deposit, and under what condition is it refunded, and within what timeframe?
Response 3 (t2-p3): Tenant responsibilities: list everything the excerpt says the tenant must do.
Response 4 (t2-p4): Notice-to-end terms: how much notice is required before moving out, and what does the excerpt say about subletting?
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: reading a sample lease and naming its obligations minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Which clause in this excerpt is one a first-time tenant might not think to look for, and why does missing it matter?

Success checks: Obligation identification accuracy: All four categories are correctly and specifically stated using details from the excerpt. | Tenant vs. landlord distinction: All listed obligations are correctly attributed to tenant or landlord. | Noticing what's easy to miss: Reflection identifies a specific clause and gives a plausible reason it's easy to miss.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: reading a sample lease and naming its obligations supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u04-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional reading a sample lease and naming its obligations condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Obligation identification accuracy: All four categories are correctly and specifically stated using details from the excerpt. | Tenant vs. landlord distinction: All listed obligations are correctly attributed to tenant or landlord. | Noticing what's easy to miss: Reflection identifies a specific clause and gives a plausible reason it's easy to miss..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.
